name: EverestIMS Technologies Limited
sector: Enterprise IT management software, implementation and hardware
summary: EverestIMS is an established Indian enterprise IT-management software vendor, not yet an evidenced high-retention SaaS compounder. It has grown consolidated revenue from ₹13.35 crore in FY21 to ₹65.12 crore in FY26, owns software and sells through partners, but most disclosed revenue is software-product sales that include upfront on-premise licences. FY26 growth slowed to 15.18%, or 5.89% excluding the new hardware line; PAT fell. The decisive research issue is whether recurring customer economics and collections justify continued development investment, not whether the company can use AI terminology. At the dated 19 October close of ₹110.60, equity value is ₹239.32 crore, reported earnings cost 18.21x and a full-development-expensing sensitivity costs about 25.05x. A conditional five-year Base model returns only 7.26% against the 15% nominal pretax hurdle, but the current funding and revenue-economics evidence is insufficient to treat even that diagnostic as an underwritten base return. Classification: speculative product-growth watchlist, not a proven compounder or a new-investment conclusion. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality) and IAS remain NS because CAP is unproven and R/L are incomplete. Reconciled post-IPO cash, independently verifiable recurring-revenue/retention economics and stronger collections could change the assessment.

gates.reason: No demonstrated severe fraud, diversion or minority abuse. Remuneration, related rent and compliance history warrant scrutiny, but corrected disclosure is not proof of intentional abuse.

Latest restated statements reconcile key PAT and CFO classifications. Subsidiary audit-reliance correction and archive/report typos reduce confidence, but no material unresolved latest-statement contradiction was found. Recurring economics remain ND, rather than fabricated.

Listing and primary issue are evidenced, but current cash-use bridge, unrestricted deposit split, April–October claims and bank renewal are missing. Synthetic positive cash does not establish current funding; no actual default or funding failure is claimed.
Eligible ST mapping and 1,600lot verified. First ten-day trade-for-trade window, incomplete eight-session history and unverified spreads/turnover constrain execution. No current suspension inferred.

GOV.reason: Audited restatements, disclosed related lease and founder ownership provide accountability. Contrary evidence is material executive remuneration relative to PAT, historical filing delays and correction of the subsidiary audit description. The final prospectus explains the changes and the subsidiary is small. Mixed stewardship is evidenced; no severe diversion, abusive financing or automatic integrity failure is established.

MOAT.reason: Owned integrated tools, implementation knowledge and customer workflow embedment plausibly create switching friction. The product has commercial revenue and an engineering team, rather than only a brand claim. Against this, partner dependence, high customer concentration, readily identified competitors and absent retention/gross-margin/cohort data prevent a demonstrated durable pricing-power moat.

REV.reason: FY21–26 consolidated revenue rises ₹13.3538 crore to ₹65.1239 crore,37.29% CAGR: schedule 9. Sustained annual deceleration and FY26 hardware contribution justify one net trajectory point deduction to 8, also the Medium-confidence maximum. FY23–26 comparable restated CAGR 23.99% is a corroborating shorter window, not cherry-picked as the primary window. No further bonus or separate hardware penalty is stacked.

DUR.reason: Existing enterprise IT operations demand, on-premise/cloud choices,230 staff and disclosed ₹39.12 crore order book establish an accessible runway. Cross-selling and software updates are plausible, but not measured expansion economics. Customer concentration, competing platforms and ₹5.66 crore uncommissioned AI hardware plan constrain duration and capture. Six is an accessible conditional runway, not a TAM score.

CAP.reason: The meaningful FY23–26 delta-NOPAT/delta-invested-capital proxy is 20.03% with ₹35.8219 crore additional capital. It cannot separate mature software cohorts, old-product repricing, FY26 hardware, accrued billings or development capitalization timing. No attributable project, unit or cohort alternative exists. Current ROCE, a good-looking accounting proxy and a neutral 5 are not substitutes: CAP remains NS.

CASH.reason: FD-flow reclassification improves three-year CFO/PAT from 45.09% to 68.85%, an important counterweight to the raw figure; older receivables improved. Yet only ₹3.648 crore remains after ₹22.5457 crore capex across three years, and FY26 adjusted FCF is negative ₹1.922 crore. EndingDSO291 days, unbilled revenue and Q4 concentration constrain genuine cash conversion. Four reflects weak but not persistently near-zero normalized operating conversion.

BAL.reason: No funded debt at 31 March, ₹60.59 crore equity and a completed primary issue are meaningful support. Against that, ₹12.0335 crore deposits are not established freely available, much operating funding sits in trade/statutory/customer liabilities, and the disclosed non-fund sanction expired before cutoff. Synthetic funded cases do not verify current liquidity. Five recognizes both support and the current-cash bridge gap; no insolvency asserted.

EXEC.reason: Management delivered a functioning product suite, revenue scale, expanded staffing and listing. The expansion hardware remains a quoted plan, not a commissioned capacity result; software-only momentum and recent PAT declined, while disclosure corrections and collection intensity weaken execution quality. Order book must be converted to collected revenue. Five reflects mixed delivery rather than treating the IPO as proof of returns.

EARN.reason: The business is profitable with relatively little other income, and FY26 operating EBITDA still grew. But PAT fell 6.66%, operating margin compressed, full-expensed-development EBIT fell and the new-share denominator reduces FY26 EPS to ₹6.07 versus historical ₹7.71. The disclosed tax/restatement bridge is reconciled. Four reflects deteriorating recent per-share earning quality rather than an accusation of invalid accounting.

R.reason: A mathematically funded Base diagnostic yields 7.26%, below the 15% hurdle, but current usable proceeds, interim claims, recurring revenue and margins are not verified sufficiently to underwrite that as the current base. The severe default path is unfunded and its ordinary return is null. Neither the 7.26% diagnostic nor the separate hypothetical rescue is scoreable R. R and IAS remain NS.

D.reason: The linked Bear path combines loss of the largest-customer equivalent, lower margin, prolonged collections, continued development spending and 12 xexit earnings; terminal value is about ₹29.91,73% below entry. A harsher 40% legacy-receivable impairment produces an early financing gap. Existing profits, fresh equity and improving aged receivables are contrary support, not a guaranteed capital floor.

P.reason: At ₹110.60,18.21x reported earnings is not an extreme SaaS multiple, but roughly 25.05 xfull-development-expensed normalized earnings offers limited protection against deceleration and weak cash conversion. Base terminal earnings need about 27.12x exit P/E to meet 15% versus 18x assumed. Four reflects an optimistic quality/collection price, not use of unverified peer multiples.

L.reason: A1,600-sharelot costs ₹176,960; ₹5 lakh fits only two lots. Observed seven-day proxy turnover suggests capacity but omits listing day and lacks a 20/60-session record, official turnover or spreads; one observed day has a single price and several near-limit changes. No stable L band can be assigned from IPO-week prints. L remains NS, not zero and not an easy-exit score.

BQS.cap_reason: No numerical cap triggered; missing factors remain NS. G3 Hold does not exclude quality by itself.
BQS.rounding: Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP for display only; no intermediate rounding.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: EverestIMS is an established Indian enterprise IT-management software vendor, not yet an evidenced high-retention SaaS compounder. It has grown consolidated revenue from ₹13.35 crore in FY21 to ₹65.12 crore in FY26, owns software and sells through partners, but most disclosed revenue is software-product sales that include upfront on-premise licences. FY26 growth slowed to 15.18%, or 5.89% excluding the new hardware line; PAT fell. The decisive research issue is whether recurring customer economics and collections justify continued development investment, not whether the company can use AI terminology. At the dated 19 October close of ₹110.60, equity value is ₹239.32 crore, reported earnings cost 18.21x and a full-development-expensing sensitivity costs about 25.05x. A conditional five-year Base model returns only 7.26% against the 15% nominal pretax hurdle, but the current funding and revenue-economics evidence is insufficient to treat even that diagnostic as an underwritten base return. Classification: speculative product-growth watchlist, not a proven compounder or a new-investment conclusion. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality) and IAS remain NS because CAP is unproven and R/L are incomplete. Reconciled post-IPO cash, independently verifiable recurring-revenue/retention economics and stronger collections could change the assessment.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity is EverestIMS Technologies Limited, incorporated 13 April 2017, converted to public limited status 10 September 2024, CIN U72900KA2017PLC102256. BSE SME identity is EIMS, code 544979, ISIN INE0YUW01020. Listing was 8 October 2026 and issue price ₹85. The primary 19 October interoperable master confirms 21,638,178 shares, ₹10 face value and a 1,600-share lot. Its EIMS$ ST row is eligible; the alternate SM row is not. This is a BSE security appearing in an NSE-maintained interoperability file, not an NSE-listed company. The copied listing notice specifies MT trade-for-trade for ten trading days. Eight exchange sessions had occurred by the dated quote, so the initial restriction should not be presumed finished.

Research cutoff is 20 October 2026. The ₹110.60 price is a secondary historical closing trade dated 19 October, not a live executable bid or a claimed official bhavcopy. Retrieval occurred 21 October, but later information is excluded. Financial anchor is consolidated Indian GAAP, year ended 31 March 2026, including wholly owned US Infraon Corp. FY21/22 older signed statements are separated from FY23–26 restated data. No retrieved H1 FY27 statement supports an interim run rate. Horizon is five years to 19 October 2031, hurdle 15% nominal pretax shareholder return, and liquidity reference ₹5 lakh, not a recommended position size.

G1 Integrity is Conditional: mixed controls without evidenced severe abuse. G2 Reliability is Conditional: the latest statements and material restatement/classification bridges are usable with qualifications. G3 Funding is Hold, because the current cash-use bridge and usable bank/deposit evidence are missing, not because an actual default is established. G4 Tradability is Conditional: eligible, but very short trading history and lot/circuit constraints.

Confidence is high on legal identity, issued capital and latest audited line items; medium on longer growth history, earnings normalization and competitive position; low on attributable incremental returns, recurring software economics, current funding and executable liquidity. These are different gaps and must not be collapsed into an allegation that all audited financials are unreliable.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV5, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP NS, CASH4, BAL5, EXEC5 and EARN4. Investment factors are RNS, D3, P4 and LNS. Each has a separate audit containing positive evidence, contrary evidence, confidence and evidence IDs. CAP is not replaced by current ROCE or the 20.03% accounting incremental-return proxy. R is not assigned from a hypothetical funded spreadsheet. L is not assigned from seven IPO-week observations.

BQS weights are GOV20%, MOAT20%, REV12%, DUR10%, CAP12%, CASH10%, BAL8%, EXEC8%. Known weighted contribution is 4.76; coverage is 88%, with CAP missing. Completion bounds are 4.88–5.96. GQS weights are REV40%, DUR20%, EARN15%, CAP15%, CASH10%; known contribution 5.40, coverage 85%, bounds 5.55–6.90. These are missing-factor completion bounds, not point scores or confidence intervals. They cannot be ranked as midpoint estimates.

IAS uses final unrounded BQS as Q25%, R35%, D20%, P10%, L10%. Q, R and L are missing, so known contribution is 1.00, coverage 30%, and canonical bounds 1.70–8.00. Propagating BQS completion bounds narrows the diagnostic range to 2.67–6.99, without producing an IAS point. All weights and contributions are computed with Decimal; display alone uses half-up rounding. No known-factor renormalization occurs.

No numerical override is activated: GOV is above 3, normalized CASH is 4 rather than mechanically scored from the misleading raw FD-inclusive ratio, and G3 is Hold rather than Fail. Quality and Growth Quality ranking exclusion follows missing CAP, not G3 Hold alone. Investment ranking also lacks a supported current base return and a canonical liquidity estimate. The shorter restated FY23–26 revenue window is disclosed as a sensitivity; the canonical REV window remains the available five-year group history with Medium confidence and a one-point deceleration deduction.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company develops the Infraon family of enterprise infrastructure monitoring, service management, asset management, AIOps and telecom operations-support products. The commercial proposition is to combine tools and workflows that an enterprise might otherwise buy separately. Products can be deployed on-premise or through the cloud. Integration, customization, implementation and ongoing support are economically different activities, even when sold under one platform name.

The prospectus explicitly describes one-time upfront per-user on-premise licence fees, additional fees for added users/products, telecom OSS customization fees and annual maintenance charges. Cloud platform subscriptions are charged annually and appear within sale of services. Therefore neither all software-product revenue nor all services can safely be called ARR. Subscription/service contracts spanning periods are deferred and recognized over their service period. The public disclosure does not quantify recurring product revenue separately from licences, maintenance, customization and implementation. It does not provide gross or net retention, renewal cohorts, average subscription contract value or product gross margin.

FY26 revenue comprises ₹50.0557 croresoftware products, ₹9.8142 croreservices and ₹5.2540 crore hardware. Those are 76.86%,15.07% and 8.07% of revenue, not recurring/non-recurring percentages. India supplied 93.96% of revenue and exports 6.04%. Sales mainly use partners and distributors; the prospectus says direct-customer licence agreements are not generally executed, while some partner agreements are formalized. This makes end-customer usage and channel receivable quality distinct research questions.

At March 2026 the company had 230 employees versus 201 a year earlier and 157 in FY24, including 107 in engineering and 59 in customer success. Such investment supports a functioning product business, but staff counts do not prove customer acquisition efficiency or incremental returns. Revenue is concentrated: the largest customer generated 29.55%, top five 76.07% and top ten 88.77%. Customer names are withheld in the prospectus. Website logos are therefore not treated as independently verified contracts or durable relationships. The ₹39.1219 crore order book at 31 August 2026 demonstrates contracted commercial activity only to the extent disclosed; execution dates, cancellations, margin and cash milestones remain unknown.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible moat mechanism is workflow embedment: monitoring history, asset configuration, ticketing processes, integration with enterprise systems and trained customer teams can make replacement disruptive. A locally supported integrated suite may win where reliability, customization and cost matter more than a premium global brand. This is stronger evidence than an idea-stage software story because the company has customers, software revenue, engineers and support staff. It remains weaker than a measured moat because retention, expansion, pricing uplift and customer lifetime profitability are not disclosed.

The strongest counterargument is that integration is also a competitive requirement. ManageEngine directly offers overlapping IT service/operations tools with on-premise/cloud choices. Freshworks has substantial service-management software operations and publishes retention and cash metrics. Newgen is broader process/content automation, not a perfect ITSM peer, but offers a useful Indian enterprise-product reporting comparator. These three are selected for business/economics comparison; they are not an arbitrary basket for importing valuation multiples.

Newgen's dated FY26 release reports ₹1,574 crore revenue, ₹968 crore annuity revenue and ₹525 croresubscription revenue, with SaaS growth 36%. Freshworks' FY2025 release reports$838.8 million revenue, reported net dollar retention 108% (104% constant currency), and$242.4 million operating cash flow. Its GAAP and non-GAAP operating margins differ sharply and cannot be substituted. ManageEngine is private and comparable public financial metrics are unavailable. EverestIMS has not provided equivalent recurring-revenue, retention or gross-margin detail, so a lower information confidence is justified without claiming its customer retention must be poor.

Concentration can be both evidence of successful enterprise deployments and a bargaining-power risk. A29.55% customer can materially influence timing, pricing and collections. Channel relationships and customization can create dependence on people rather than product-level network effects. There is no quantified market share, independent replacement-cost study, patent-based exclusivity or audited product cohort that establishes an enduring high-return moat. MOAT5 therefore recognizes useful embedment while requiring evidence that it survives price competition, AI-driven product change and loss of a major channel/customer.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The available consolidated series is FY21₹13.3538 crore, FY22₹22.8572 crore, FY23₹34.1670 crore, FY24₹45.2280 crore, FY25₹56.5430 crore and FY26₹65.1239 crore. FY21/22 are rounded-thousand signed statements, not later restated lakhs. The archive filename is misleading; the FY22 body, date and signatures were visually verified. FY23 comes from the earlier DRHP, while final-prospectus FY24/25 figures supersede earlier versions. The wholly owned US subsidiary existed from March 2021; it is not a recent large acquisition explanation for FY26 growth.

FY2022: revenue ₹22.8572 crore; increase ₹9.5034 crore; growth 71.17%.
FY2023: revenue ₹34.1670 crore; increase ₹11.3098 crore; growth 49.48%.
FY2024: revenue ₹45.2280 crore; increase ₹11.0610 crore; growth 32.37%.
FY2025: revenue ₹56.5430 crore; increase ₹11.3150 crore; growth 25.02%.
FY2026: revenue ₹65.1239 crore; increase ₹8.5809 crore; growth 15.18%.

Five-year CAGR is 37.29%; the stricter FY23–26 restated three-year CAGR is 23.99%. Absolute annual additions peaked at ₹11.315 crore in FY25 and declined to ₹8.5809 crore in FY26. This is not merely percentage deceleration from a rising denominator. FY26 hardware, absent in FY25, supplied ₹5.254 crore, approximately 61.23% of the incremental revenue. Excluding hardware, revenue rose only 5.89%. Software products rose 4.33%, while services rose 14.61%. FY26 supplier concentration includes one supplier representing 60.92% of purchases; its disclosed purchase amount is close to hardware revenue, but that coincidence is not a verified hardware gross-margin allocation.

Growth is lumpy. FY26 revenue by quarter was ₹0.3699 crore, ₹23.1188 crore, ₹4.8511 crore and ₹36.7841 crore;56.48% arrived in Q4. H1 grew about 2.36% and H2 about 23.93%, but no quarterly hardware split permits a clean underlying acceleration claim. Q4 must not be multiplied by four. The latest available fiscal year is the TTM anchor; no current interim result is inserted.

Price versus user volume, new logos versus renewals, channel sell-through versus inventory and acquisition versus internal growth are not fully bridged. The REV score uses the prescribed five-year schedule 9, then one net point for sustained deceleration, with the Medium-confidence ceiling also 8. This recognizes real historic scaling without pretending the current software run rate is still expanding at 37%.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Bottom-up demand access is more credible than a market-size extrapolation: existing enterprise deployments can add modules/users, support can renew, cloud subscriptions can expand, and a 230-person team can sell and deliver additional projects. The disclosed ₹39.12 crore order book is about 60% of FY26 revenue, but does not tell us how much is incremental, recurring, high-margin or cash-backed. It cannot simply be added to existing annual revenue because some orders may replace normal business or span years.

Reinvestment is already material. FY26 in-house software additions were ₹9.0313 crore,13.87% of revenue, compared with ₹5.0763 crore amortization. The IPO additionally earmarks ₹5.6556 crore for hardware infrastructure, ₹24 crore for working capital and ₹5.4932 crore for general corporate purposes. Hardware procurement was supported by quotations rather than delivered assets or a commissioned productivity record. Associated GST, freight and installation can require internal cash. No independent project appraisal or attributable incremental revenue return is supplied.

The reconstructed operating invested-capital base rises from ₹13.1193 crore in FY23 to ₹48.9412 crore in FY26. At a consistent 26% tax assumption, operating NOPAT rises by ₹7.175336 crore over ₹35.8219 crore additional capital, an accounting incremental proxy of 20.03%. The denominator is meaningful, not near zero. Yet the numerator combines mature licence economics, pricing/mix, hardware and accruals; the denominator combines receivables, capitalized code and operating funding. There is no dated cohort showing what the incremental software investment itself earned. A12–16% cost-of-capital sensitivity makes the proxy look potentially attractive, but that analytical range is not a measured company WACC and does not repair attribution. CAP remains NS.

The five-year diagnostic Base requires software-product growth 10%, services 14%, hardware flat,14% of revenue reinvested in development and improved ending receivable days. Those assumptions are intentionally visible, not management guidance or an underwritten forecast. GQS remains NS at 85% coverage. No CASH≤3 cap is triggered because normalized cash conversion has real positive counterevidence, but weak residual cash and capital intensity limit confidence that growth is self-funding. Required proof is renewal/cohort economics, commissioned project outcomes and a current cash-use bridge, not more TAM or AI narrative.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder leadership includes managing director Satish Kumar Vijayaragavan, chairman Sudhakar Aruchamy and six other promoter executives. Post-offer promoter ownership is 58.98%, down from 80.38% before the offer through new shares and promoter secondary sales. The OFS ₹9.4112 crore goes to sellers and is not company funding. The prospectus reports no outstanding warrants, options or convertible instruments at filing; the historical ESOP share issuance is already in the pre-IPO share count. Future dilution is possible but is not silently included as free funding.

Disclosed FY26 remuneration and benefits for eight promoter directors total ₹5.078 crore, approximately 38.65% of PAT. That is a substantial economic claim requiring comparison with operating responsibility, not an automatic finding of excess or diversion. Several directors changed roles in FY25, so reported director-only FY24 remuneration is not a clean all-management-pay comparator. Vedanshi Infotech, connected through director Ramesh Pratap Tiwari, received ₹0.0819 crore rent. A September 2026 non-compete arrangement is disclosed. The rent is small relative to revenue, but independent lease terms and related-business boundaries still matter.

The prospectus reports historic RoC filing delays of 1–69 days and corrected allotment forms. Tax-payment delays include FY24 TDS ₹17.02 lakh for 22 days and small later items. The disclosed promoter/director tax proceedings are small; there is no basis here to recast them as a material company lawsuit. These facts justify monitoring control quality, not a severe integrity-failure gate.

Promises versus delivery: the company built software and grew staff/revenue through March 2026; the primary issue and October listing were completed; the 31 August order book is a dated management disclosure, not collected revenue; the proposed AI hardware has quotations but no evidenced commissioning by cutoff. The HDFC sanction disclosed through 30 September 2026 requires renewal evidence. Its expired document is not proof the bank declined renewal.

The 5 October corrigendum matters: it corrects which firm audited the parent and clarifies that US subsidiary accounts were audited by SH&Co, while management supplied unaudited IGAAP conversions. Final disclosure and small subsidiary scale temper the issue, but the correction should not disappear from the governance record. GOV5 and EXEC5 reflect mixed, observable stewardship and delivery rather than either promotional confidence or an unsupported fraud allegation.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2023: revenue ₹34.17 crore; PAT ₹5.50 crore; operating EBITDA ₹8.97 crore; reported CFO ₹3.60 crore; total capex ₹4.14 crore; invested capital ₹13.12 crore.
FY2024: revenue ₹45.23 crore; PAT ₹10.83 crore; operating EBITDA ₹17.30 crore; reported CFO ₹5.32 crore; total capex ₹5.50 crore; invested capital ₹26.66 crore.
FY2025: revenue ₹56.54 crore; PAT ₹14.08 crore; operating EBITDA ₹21.42 crore; reported CFO ₹2.63 crore; total capex ₹7.55 crore; invested capital ₹35.02 crore.
FY2026: revenue ₹65.12 crore; PAT ₹13.14 crore; operating EBITDA ₹22.57 crore; reported CFO ₹9.20 crore; total capex ₹9.49 crore; invested capital ₹48.94 crore.

Operating EBIT is PBT plus all finance expense less other income; operating EBITDA adds depreciation/amortization. This differs slightly from the issuer's adjusted EBITDA because LC-discounting charges are included consistently as financing costs here. FY26 operating EBITDA ₹22.5676 crore is 34.65% of revenue; employee and implementation costs are not split by function, so revenue minus purchased goods/services is not a defensible product gross margin. FY26 PAT ₹13.1393 crore fell 6.66% despite revenue growth. Other income ₹0.7908 crore is modest, but FY25 included mutual-fund gains and provision reversal. Audited FY26 PAT ₹13.1865 crore reconciles to restated PAT through ₹0.0472 crore tax; FY25/FY24 reclassifications are separately retained. A misprinted other-income note total is reconciled to components and the P&L, not left as unexplained unreliability.

Reported FY24–26 CFO totals ₹17.1571 crore versus PAT ₹38.0471 crore,45.09%. However, movements into/outof fixed deposits sit inside the statement's other-current/non-current asset flows. TotalFDs were ₹2.9969/₹2.3266/₹13.6624/₹12.0335 crore at FY23/24/25/26. Adding the change in totalFDs to each reported CFO yields ₹4.6545/₹13.9665/₹7.5727 crore, a three-year ratio 68.85%. This is a classification correction, not cash creation. Deduct total capex ₹22.5457 crore once to obtain ₹3.6480 crore cumulativeFCF. FY26 adjustedFCF is negative ₹1.9220 crore. Restricted FDs do not become available funding merely because their movements are removed from CFO.

Development is capitalized after stated marketing-feasibility criteria and amortized over three years. Full-expensing sensitivity subtracts new in-house additions and adds back their amortization. FY26 EBIT falls from ₹16.8648 crore to ₹12.9098 crore; at 26% tax this is ₹9.553252 crore normalized operating earnings. This is a conservative alternative presentation, not an allegation of incorrect statutory accounting. Cash used for development is already inside capex, and is not deducted again from FCF. The corresponding development-expensed operating-cash view is separately reported.

Receivables rose to ₹51.962 crore plus ₹2.6269 crore unbilled. Ending DSO is 291 days; issuer 249 days uses average receivables and is not contradictory. Important contrary evidence: receivables older than six months fell from ₹13.2987 crore to ₹4.4993 crore. The question is subsequent collection of the much larger fresh billings, especially Q4, not an assertion every debtor worsened.

Operating invested capital includes PPE, intangibles, operating deposits, receivables, unbilled and advances, less operating payables/provisions, with tax provision excluded. It reconciles to equity plusDTL/long-term provisions less financial assets and non-operating tax/interest assets. FY26₹48.9412 crore is reproducible on both sides. Current returns on that capital are context only; incremental attribution remains NS. There was no funded debt at March, so an enormous EBIT/LC-charge ratio is not promoted as meaningful interest coverage. Cash equivalents ₹2.5661 crore, FDs ₹12.0335 crore and mutual funds ₹0.7586 crore are kept separate. Shares increase from 17,044,578 to 21,638,178 after the primary issue; current-share FY26 EPS is ₹6.07, not the historical ₹7.71.

For context only, FY26 operating NOPAT at the analytical 26% tax rate is ₹12.4800 crore on average invested capital ₹41.9815 crore, or 29.73% average-capital ROIC. This current accounting return is not the CAP score: the meaningful three-year incremental accounting proxy is 20.03%, and neither measure identifies what the new software-development cohorts themselves earned.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹110.60 and 21,638,178 shares, marketcap is ₹239.3182 crore. Historical PE on current shares is 18.21x, and the full-development-expensing sensitivity is 25.05x. EV deducting only March cash equivalents is ₹236.7521 crore or 10.49x operating EBITDA. Assuming every estimated net IPO rupee remained unspent would reduceEV to ₹201.6033 crore, but that is not a verified currentEV. FDs, mutual funds, IPO proceeds and opening liabilities are not indiscriminately netted. Book value multiples likewise range from 3.95x March equity to 2.50 xif estimated net IPO proceeds were added without other changes; the latter is explicitly pro forma.

Method is five-year operating-earnings valuation plus excess cash, cross-checked against reinvestment and annual financing. The model uses 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031 anniversaries and FY26 as the last known run-rate anchor, not a fabricated October TTM. Opening cash is synthetic:₹2.5661 crore March cash plus ₹35.1488 crore estimated net primary IPO, less ₹17.5035 crore opening trade/employee/statutory/short-provision claims, giving ₹20.2114 crore. Settled claims are removed from opening working-capital liabilities, so their payment cannot be charged again through working-capital changes. Customer advances remain operating funding. No cash is supplied from the ₹22 crore non-fund line or unverified deposit releases.

The ₹24 crore working-capital IPO object is an allocation, not a separate expense: modeled changes in receivables, unbilled, advances, customer advances and new trade payables consume or release cash. Year 1 hardware capex ₹5.6556 crore is additional to 1% annual physical capex;18% GST is an explicit timing buffer recovered in year 2. General-purpose ₹5.4932 crore is conservatively spent and expensed once in year 1. Development investment 13–16% of revenue is separately amortized in three-year cohorts. Tax 26%, debt/interest/dividends zero and minimum cash ₹2 crore are explicit. Terminal PE values operating PAT, excludes interest income, and adds only cash above the buffer. Existing FDs are neither funding nor terminal windfalls.

Bear: year 5 revenue ₹47.47 crore, PAT ₹2.97 crore, exit PE12.0x, terminal price ₹29.91, conditionalIRR-23.02%, minimum cash ₹15.80 crore.
Base: year 5 revenue ₹104.77 crore, PAT ₹15.52 crore, exit PE18.0x, terminal price ₹157.05, conditionalIRR 7.26%, minimum cash ₹19.61 crore.
Bull: year 5 revenue ₹147.75 crore, PAT ₹27.69 crore, exit PE24.0x, terminal price ₹346.72, conditionalIRR 25.67%, minimum cash ₹20.21 crore.

Bear loses the largest-customer equivalent in software/services, excludes repeat hardware and keeps receivable days 330–365. Base grows products 10%, services 14%, holds hardware flat and reduces ending DSO275 to 230. Bull grows products 18%, services 22%, improves margins and DSO250 to 180. These are conditional diagnostics, not probabilities or supported forecasts. Base requires roughly 27.12x terminal PE instead of 18x to achieve the 15% hurdle, or ₹23.38 crore terminal PAT at 18x after assumed excess cash. Exit P/E sensitivities 12–24x are retained. A purely algebraic 15%-hurdle entry is about ₹78.08 using Base terminal value, but it is not a supportable buy price until funding and recurring economics are evidenced. R remains NS; price alone cannot repair those gaps.

Liquidity is separately constrained. Seven observed sessions have mean close-times-volume proxy turnover ₹3.1456 crore and median ₹2.7755 crore; the lower median is the illustrative denominator, not official traded value. For the nominal ₹5 lakh reference, the 2%/5%/10% proxy liquidation estimates are 0.90/0.36/0.18 days. Whole lots prevent investing exactly ₹5 lakh: two lots are ₹353,920, three ₹530,880. At 5% participation, observed daily volume allows only 2–22 complete lots, with two at the weakest observed session; a single-price session can still prevent the desired side from executing. The 8 October listing session is missing, not zero. No 20/60-session record, bid-ask spread or depth is available. The roughly 41.02% non-promoter share is not verified freely tradable float because lock-ins and market-maker inventory matter. These short-window calculations are diagnostics only: L remains NS and implementation requires current quote/lot/restriction checks.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that software has no demand. It is that a concentrated, partly upfront licence model is mistaken for self-funding recurring SaaS just as underlying growth slows. Lose a major enterprise/channel relationship, and new licence revenue falls while product development and support staff cannot be cut proportionately. Acceptance and payment delays extend already long receivable days. Capitalized development then both consumes cash and creates future amortization/impairment risk. A lower exit multiple compounds lower earnings.

The linked Bear diagnostic removes 29.55% of first-year software/services revenue, assumes no repeat hardware,23–27% EBITDA margins before the specified one-off spend,365-to 330 ending DSO,16% development investment and 12 xexit PE. It also assumes 10% of legacy receivables never convert to cash. It remains cash-funded under the synthetic March-plus-IPO opening, but terminal price is only ₹29.91 versus ₹110.60, a 73% capital decline. That is a scenario, not a forecast or probability-weighted target. The fresh primary issue and aged-receivable improvement are genuine counterarguments and explain why the moderate Bear need not imply bankruptcy.

A separate severe collection-default stress raises legacy receivable impairment to 40% and lowers operating margins. The first-year cash trough is negative ₹1.05 crore; maintaining the ₹2 crore buffer requires ₹3.0525 crore additional funding. Its ordinary IRR and upside are null despite positive terminal algebra, because it cannot reach that endpoint without a financing event. The separate hypothetical equity rescue raises ₹3.2131 crore gross at ₹88.48, pays 5% fees and adds about 363,149 shares; existing-holder five-year IRR is approximately negative 32.29%. No committed buyer exists. This rescue is not mixed into the ordinary Base or used forR/G3.

Tangible accounting equity before IPO is about ₹46.28 crore, roughly ₹21.39 per share on the post-offer share count, and even that depends heavily on collectible receivables. Software book value is not an independent liquidation floor. IPO proceeds, if still available, improve recovery, but cannot be counted both as spendable growth funding and untouched cash protection. The thesis-break variables are sustained major-customer churn, inability to collect recent billing, repeated development capitalization without product cash returns, or an adverse current funding reconciliation. No such future failure is asserted as a known present fact.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold stock outcome over five years requires 37.97% annual return; tenfold requires 58.49%. Over ten years the requirements are 17.46% and 25.89%, respectively. These arithmetic hurdles differ from revenue CAGR because margin, valuation, cash generation and dilution all matter. A low starting marketcap is not a causal route to either outcome.

At unchanged share count,5×equity value would be ₹1,196.59 crore and 10×₹2,393.18 crore. At 20x terminal earnings with no extra cash credit, those values require PAT ₹59.83 crore and ₹119.66 crore. At 20% net margin, required revenue is ₹299.15 crore and ₹598.30 crore, implying 35.65% and 55.82% five-year revenue CAGR from FY26. The 20% margin is an explicit favorable assumption, particularly after recognizing development costs and the FY26 hardware mix. More dilution or lower terminal valuation increases the required operating scale.

Current evidence does not justify either as a base case. The company has achieved 37.29% historical five-year revenue CAGR from a much smaller base, but annual growth has decelerated and FY26 ex-hardware growth is 5.89%. The conditional Bull reaches only ₹147.75 crore revenue and ₹27.69 crore PAT by year 5; even at 24 x earnings plus modeled cash, its price is ₹346.72, about 3.14×entry. Extending that path for another five years requires continuing demand capture, customer diversification, attractive incremental returns and funding that have not yet been demonstrated.

A credible 5×case would require evidence of recurring product expansion, repeatable channel/customer acquisition economics, cash-backed renewal growth and the ability to scale development more slowly than revenue without losing competitiveness. A10×five-year case would require an even larger discontinuity. Neither an AI hardware purchase nor a large sectorTAM establishes those facts. These outcomes remain speculative possibilities, not scored promises or an excuse to ignore the 15% required-return test.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Current liquidity bridge. Obtain 31 March-to 20 October cash movement, net IPO receipt/utilization and a deposit restriction schedule. Baselines are ₹2.5661 crore cash equivalents, ₹12.0335 crore FDs and estimated ₹35.1488 crore net primary proceeds. Resolve before lifting G3 Hold or assigning R; a reconciliation that uses the same IPO rupee for multiple purposes is unacceptable.

2. Software revenue quality. Request licence, subscription, AMC, implementation/customization and hardware splits. FY26 baselines are ₹50.0557/₹9.8142/₹5.2540 crore for published product/services/hardware categories. Track ARR, gross retention and net retention with definitions and cohorts. Do not impose a 100% NRR threshold on a licence metric; first establish a valid recurring denominator.

3. Collections. Baselines are ₹51.962 crore receivables, ₹2.6269 crore unbilled,291 ending DSO and ₹4.4993 crore overdue beyond six months. Subsequent collections of March/Q4 invoices are more informative than aggregate assurance. Ending DSO persistently above 300 or renewed over-six-month growth is a warning; actual write-offs or stalled major customer receipts can break the thesis.

4. Concentration and order book. Follow largest customer 29.55%, top five 76.07%, and ₹39.1219 crore 31 August order book. Require dated conversion, cancellations and collected cash, not only book replenishment. A major customer loss without replacement is a scenario trigger, not an automatic prediction.

5. Development economics. Baseline ₹9.0313 crore FY26 capitalized development and ₹5.0763 crore amortization. Ask for product/cohort spend, launch dates, revenue, gross profit and maintenance burden. Capitalization continuing above cash growth without attributable returns keeps CAP NS; unexplained impairment or shorter useful lives weakens EARN/CASH.

6. IPO execution. Verify hardware orders, invoice values, commissioning and utilization against ₹5.6556 crore plan, with GST/freight cash. Reconcile ₹24 crore working-capital allocation to actual balance changes. Do not treat spend as proof of economic return.

7. Bank and obligations. Confirm renewal of the HDFC sanction beyond 30 September 2026, drawings, eligible LCs, margin FDs and covenants. Non-fund limit ₹22 crore is not fungible cash. Watch statutory/MSME payments and any shift to expensive demand debt.

8. Per-share results and governance. Use 21,638,178 shares unless a verified change occurs; monitor new options, related transactions, director pay, auditor language and corrections. FY26 current-share EPS ₹6.07 is the proper baseline.

9. Tradability. Obtain official BSE turnover, full post-listing calendar, spreads and depths after 20 and 60 sessions are available. Recheck lot/circuit/surveillance status before implementation. Calculate 2%,5%,10% whole-lot capacity for the actual position, not only ₹5 lakh. Monitoring is a research plan, not a standing authorization to trade or an automation claim.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
The appropriate classification is speculative enterprise-product growth watchlist with unresolved underwriting, not a proven compounder, income stock, asset-backed bargain or turnaround. There is a real operating business and credible historical scaling, but the combination of slowing underlying growth, development capitalization, concentrated billings and incomplete current funding prevents a high-conviction quality-growth conclusion. A debt-free historical balance is a strength, not a substitute for current available cash.

BQS and GQS are NS because CAP cannot be scored from attributable incremental economics. This is an evidence limitation, not a statement that actual incremental returns must be poor. IAS is separately NS because the final quality point, supported current baseIRR and canonical liquidity score are missing. G3 Hold does not, by itself, invalidate a potentially complete BQS/GQS; here the quality exclusion follows CAP. There is no severe integrity Fail or funding Fail in the gate register.

At the dated ₹110.60 price, the model's conditional Base returns 7.26%, materially below the 15% hurdle. The stock therefore does not become a buy merely because reportedPE18.21x looks modest beside global SaaS names. The normalized development-expense sensitivity and recent deceleration make that comparison fragile. A lower price could improve economics, but it cannot make an unverified funding bridge or retention metric verified. The algebraic entry cross-check is not a trading recommendation.

Next action is evidence acquisition and reconciliation, not order placement: verify post-IPO cash and restricted deposits; obtain recurring-revenue/retention and product/cohort economics; confirm collections and commissioning; then re-run the same model and score rules. If those establish durable cash-backed returns and the price offers a supported 15% baseIRR with acceptable downside, the classification can improve. If customer loss, write-offs or funding claims invalidate the bridge, downgrade on that evidence. No transaction is authorized or performed by this research artifact.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The primary anchor is the company's 6 October 2026 final prospectus, with printed-page locators and locally retained page extracts. It supersedes the 21 September RHP and older DRHP for FY24–26. The 5 October corrigendum is retained because auditor reliance and shareholder count corrections matter. The September 2025 DRHP supplies FY23. Signed FY22 consolidated statements and FY21 comparatives are taken from the actual document body, not its misnamed 2020–21 archive file. Key pages were visually checked, and older cash flow classifications are not pooled with the restated three-year conversion ratio.

Official interoperability master rows establish identity, issued capital and current lot/eligibility. The master codebook is retained to avoid mistaking the ineligible SM row for the eligible ST row. The official BSE listing page returned AccessDenied; a dated NoticeBlue reproduction is therefore explicitly secondary, corroborated against the prospectus/master. Equitypandit's 7 historical OHLCV rows are secondary, and the missing 8 October row is not inferred zero. No official BSE daily turnover or reliable bid/ask spread was retrieved. The 20/60-session liquidity score remains NS; pre-listing days are not trading zeros.

Newgen and Freshworks dated primary releases support business/reporting comparisons, not present peer prices. ManageEngine's undated official catalogue supports only product overlap. The company archive snapshot is a discovery ledger and not proof that every exchange announcement was available. No post 20 October event or 21 October price is used.

All financial models use crores except shares and per-share prices. Revenue CAGR uses actual endpoints; CFO/PAT is a ratio of sums. Operating EBIT excludes other income and includes finance expense add-back consistently. FDs are reclassified for operating cash analysis but excluded from funding until availability is proven. IC is reconciled from operating assets/liabilities and funding sources. Incremental NOPAT uses 26% analytical tax; cost of capital 12–16% is sensitivity, not a company fact. Development full-expensing is an alternative economic view, not restated audited earnings.

Forward models explicitly label synthetic opening cash, growth/margins, receivable days, development/physical capex, tax, GST timing, share count and exit multiples. Opening claims are paid once and removed from opening WC; OFS is excluded; the ₹24 crore WC object is not charged again; rescue financing is segregated. Missing current finance, customer cohorts and liquidity prevent the models from becoming R/IAS scores. The largest open questions are net proceeds actually available, interim cash use, FD restrictions/bank renewal, recurring mix/retention/gross margin, order book terms and attributable development returns. Each has a named monitoring test rather than a default neutral score.
